{"title":"NW-5809 complaint rate: September vs October 2026","sql":"WITH `monthly_metrics` AS (
  SELECT
    `month_start`,
    `complaint_count`,
    `shipment_count`,
    `complaint_count` / NULLIF(`shipment_count`, 0) AS `complaint_rate`
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', `opened_date`) AS `month_start`,
      COUNT(*) AS `complaint_count`,
      (
        SELECT COUNT(*)
        FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments` AS s
        WHERE s.`network_id` = 'NW-5809'
          AND s.`is_test` = FALSE
          AND DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', s.`ship_date`) = DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', c.`opened_date`)
      ) AS `shipment_count`
    FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`complaints` AS c
    WHERE c.`network_id` = 'NW-5809'
      AND c.`opened_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
      AND c.`opened_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', `opened_date`)
  )
),
`comparison` AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month_start` = DATE '2026-09-01' THEN `complaint_count` END) AS `september_complaints`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month_start` = DATE '2026-09-01' THEN `shipment_count` END) AS `september_shipments`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month_start` = DATE '2026-09-01' THEN `complaint_rate` END) AS `september_rate`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month_start` = DATE '2026-10-01' THEN `complaint_count` END) AS `october_complaints`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month_start` = DATE '2026-10-01' THEN `shipment_count` END) AS `october_shipments`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month_start` = DATE '2026-10-01' THEN `complaint_rate` END) AS `october_rate`
  FROM `monthly_metrics`
)
SELECT
  `september_complaints`,
  `september_shipments`,
  `september_rate`,
  `october_complaints`,
  `october_shipments`,
  `october_rate`,
  `october_rate` - `september_rate` AS `rate_change` ,
  CASE
    WHEN `october_rate` > `september_rate` THEN 'WORSENED'
    WHEN `october_rate` < `september_rate` THEN 'IMPROVED'
    ELSE 'UNCHANGED'
  END AS `conclusion`
FROM `comparison`"}

question: For network NW-7712, compare the average delivery time in September and October 2026 for customer shipments only, leaving out internal test parcels (is_test). Did delivery time improve?

item.name: execute_sql
item.arguments:
{"title":"NW-7712 September vs October delivery time","sql":"WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-10-01' THEN 'September 2026'
      WHEN `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-10-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01' THEN 'October 2026'
    END AS `month`,
    AVG(`delivery_days`) AS `average_delivery_days`,
    COUNT(*) AS `shipment_count`
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments`
  WHERE `network_id` = 'NW-7712'
    AND `is_test` = FALSE
    AND `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
    AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY CASE
    WHEN `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-10-01' THEN 'September 2026'
    WHEN `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-10-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01' THEN 'October 2026'
  END
), paired AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = 'September 2026' THEN `average_delivery_days` END) AS `september_average_delivery_days`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = 'October 2026' THEN `average_delivery_days` END) AS `october_average_delivery_days`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = 'September 2026' THEN `shipment_count` END) AS `september_shipments`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = 'October 2026' THEN `shipment_count` END) AS `october_shipments`
  FROM monthly
)
SELECT
  `september_average_delivery_days`,
  `october_average_delivery_days`,
  `october_average_delivery_days` - `september_average_delivery_days` AS `change_october_minus_september_days`,
  `september_shipments`,
  `october_shipments`,
  CASE
    WHEN `october_average_delivery_days` < `september_average_delivery_days` THEN 'Yes'
    WHEN `october_average_delivery_days` > `september_average_delivery_days` THEN 'No'
    ELSE 'No change'
  END AS `delivery_time_improved`
FROM paired"}

It rose from 3.2% in September to 5.8% in October, an increase of 2.6 percentage points, or about 81% relative. \[[1](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca1291730bbfa6b4f16622061/chats/01f1d52f0c9b1ae3a06188334bcc5aaf?gra_focus=pub_toolu_bdrk_01WE2r4tooTWhwQsE49xg4xP)\]

- **September:** 32 complaints on 1,000 shipments, a rate of 3.2%.
- **October:** 58 complaints on 1,000 shipments, a rate of 5.8%.

Shipment volume was the same in both months, so the rise comes from more complaints, not from a change in the number of shipments. There were no internal test parcels and no duplicate rows in either month, so the figures aren't distorted. The network also has no logged routing changes, so I can't point to one as a cause. \[[2](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca1291730bbfa6b4f16622061/chats/01f1d52f0c9b1ae3a06188334bcc5aaf?gra_focus=pub_toolu_bdrk_01K1wSt83pTc2UjXVEVVv8me)\]

I measured the rate as complaints opened in the month divided by shipments shipped in that month. I did not look into why complaints rose.

question: For network NW-2290, compare shipment volume in September and October 2026. Check which dates each month's data covers, and compare shipments per day. Did volume fall?

item.name: execute_sql
item.arguments:
{"title":"NW-2290 September vs October 2026 shipment volume","sql":"WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-10-01' THEN 'September 2026'
      WHEN `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-10-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01' THEN 'October 2026'
    END AS `month`,
    MIN(`ship_date`) AS `first_ship_date`,
    MAX(`ship_date`) AS `last_ship_date`,
    COUNT(*) AS `shipment_volume`,
    COUNT(DISTINCT `ship_date`) AS `active_ship_dates`
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments`
  WHERE `network_id` = 'NW-2290'
    AND `is_test` = FALSE
    AND `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
    AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY CASE
    WHEN `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-10-01' THEN 'September 2026'
    WHEN `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-10-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01' THEN 'October 2026'
  END
), metrics AS (
  SELECT
    `month`,
    `first_ship_date`,
    `last_ship_date`,
    `shipment_volume`,
    `active_ship_dates`,
    DATEDIFF(`last_ship_date`, `first_ship_date`) + 1 AS `calendar_days_covered`,
    `shipment_volume` / (DATEDIFF(`last_ship_date`, `first_ship_date`) + 1.0) AS `shipments_per_calendar_day`
  FROM monthly
), comparison AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = 'September 2026' THEN `shipment_volume` END) AS `september_volume`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = 'October 2026' THEN `shipment_volume` END) AS `october_volume`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = 'September 2026' THEN `shipments_per_calendar_day` END) AS `september_per_day`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = 'October 2026' THEN `shipments_per_calendar_day` END) AS `october_per_day`
  FROM metrics
)
SELECT
  `month`,
  `first_ship_date`,
  `last_ship_date`,
  `shipment_volume`,
  `active_ship_dates`,
  `calendar_days_covered`,
  ROUND(`shipments_per_calendar_day`, 2) AS `shipments_per_calendar_day`,
  CASE
    WHEN `month` = 'October 2026' THEN `october_volume` - `september_volume`
  END AS `volume_change`,
  CASE
    WHEN `month` = 'October 2026' AND `september_volume` <> 0
      THEN ROUND(100.0 * (`october_volume` - `september_volume`) / `september_volume`, 2)
  END AS `volume_change_pct`,
  CASE
    WHEN `month` = 'October 2026' THEN ROUND(`october_per_day` - `september_per_day`, 2)
  END AS `per_day_change`,
  CASE
    WHEN `month` = 'October 2026' AND `september_per_day` <> 0
      THEN ROUND(100.0 * (`october_per_day` - `september_per_day`) / `september_per_day`, 2)
  END AS `per_day_change_pct`
FROM metrics
CROSS JOIN comparison
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `month` = 'September 2026' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END"}

question: For network NW-7712, compare the average delivery time in September and October 2026 for customer shipments only, leaving out internal test parcels (is_test). Did delivery time improve?

item.name: execute_sql
item.arguments:
{"title":"NW-7712 September vs October delivery time","sql":"WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_FORMAT(`ship_date`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `month`,
    AVG(`delivery_days`) AS `avg_delivery_days`
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments`
  WHERE `network_id` = 'NW-7712'
    AND `is_test` = FALSE
    AND `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
    AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(`ship_date`, 'yyyy-MM')
), comparison AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = '2026-09' THEN `avg_delivery_days` END) AS `september_avg_delivery_days`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `month` = '2026-10' THEN `avg_delivery_days` END) AS `october_avg_delivery_days`
  FROM monthly
)
SELECT
  `september_avg_delivery_days`,
  `october_avg_delivery_days`,
  `october_avg_delivery_days` - `september_avg_delivery_days` AS `change_days_october_minus_september`,
  CASE
    WHEN `october_avg_delivery_days` < `september_avg_delivery_days` THEN 'Yes'
    WHEN `october_avg_delivery_days` > `september_avg_delivery_days` THEN 'No'
    ELSE 'No change'
  END AS `delivery_time_improved`
FROM comparison"}

# NW-7351 complaints, September to October 2026

**Complaints are not getting worse on a per-shipment basis. The count rose from 40 to 60, but shipment volume doubled, so the complaint rate fell from 4.0 to 3.0 per 100 shipments.** \[[1](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca3d01b7fa19459fa7b3aa43d/chats/01f1d52f2aa7184fbc5b9f750e115871?gra_focus=pub_toolu_bdrk_01LfrNQvM4o4awXVoZiCk3hy)\] \[[2](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca3d01b7fa19459fa7b3aa43d/chats/01f1d52f2aa7184fbc5b9f750e115871?gra_focus=pub_toolu_bdrk_01HGoJy9zqYdPJJA4iGyiDNi)\]

- **Rate:** The rate fell by 25% (4.0 to 3.0 complaints per 100 shipments). It fell by the same amount in both local and remote zones, so the change is not driven by one zone.

WITH s AS (SELECT date_format(ship_date,'yyyy-MM') m, service_zone z, COUNT(shipment_id) shipments FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`shipments` WHERE network_id='NW-7351' AND ship_date>='2026-09-01' GROUP BY 1,2),
c AS (SELECT date_format(sh.ship_date,'yyyy-MM') m, sh.service_zone z, COUNT(DISTINCT c.complaint_id) complaints FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`complaints` c JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`shipments` sh ON c.shipment_id=sh.shipment_id WHERE c.network_id='NW-7351' AND sh.ship_date>='2026-09-01' GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT s.m AS ship_month, s.z AS service_zone, s.shipments, COALESCE(c.complaints,0) AS complaints, ROUND(COALESCE(c.complaints,0)*100.0/s.shipments,2) AS complaints_per_100_shipments
FROM s LEFT JOIN c ON s.m=c.m AND s.z=c.z ORDER BY 1,2

question: Did delivery performance in network NW-7712 improve from September to October 2026? Support your conclusion.

item.arguments:
{"title":"NW-7712 overall delivery performance","sql":"SELECT
  date_format(`ship_date`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `shipment_month`,
  COUNT(*) AS `shipments`,
  ROUND(AVG(`delivery_days`), 2) AS `avg_delivery_days`,
  ROUND(percentile_approx(`delivery_days`, 0.5), 2) AS `median_delivery_days`,
  ROUND(AVG(`delay_days`), 2) AS `avg_delay_days`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `delay_days` = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `on_time_shipments`,

  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN `delay_days` > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS `late_rate_pct`
FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments`
WHERE `network_id` = 'NW-7712'
  AND `is_test` = FALSE
  AND `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
  AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
GROUP BY date_format(`ship_date`, 'yyyy-MM')
ORDER BY `shipment_month`"}

content.text:
Yesâdelivery performance improved in NW-7712 from September to October 2026, specifically through faster deliveries rather than improved punctuality.

- Average delivery time fell from **5.0 to 4.0 days** and the median fell from **4 to 3 days**âa one-day improvement on both measures. \[[1](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca1291730bbfa6b4f16622061/chats/01f1d52f2b021d509ec5f86294db7198?gra_focus=pub_call_n4yzoLfL5NRS1XyMy2hydUCe)\]
- The improvement was broad-based: in September, shipments were split evenly between **4 and 6 days**; in October, they were split evenly between **3 and 5 days**. Thus, both observed delivery-time groups shifted one day faster, rather than the average being driven by a small outlier group.

question: For network NW-5809, compare the complaint rate in September and October 2026 overall and within each service zone, and each zone's share of shipments. What do they show?

item.name: execute_sql
item.arguments:
{"title":"NW-5809 complaint rate and zone share, Sep-Oct 2026","sql":"WITH ship_m AS (
  SELECT date_format(`ship_date`, 'yyyy-MM') AS ym, `service_zone`, COUNT(*) AS shipments
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments`
  WHERE `network_id` = 'NW-5809' AND `is_test` = FALSE
    AND `ship_date` >= DATE'2026-09-01' AND `ship_date` < DATE'2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
comp_m AS (
  SELECT date_format(c.`opened_date`, 'yyyy-MM') AS ym, s.`service_zone`, COUNT(*) AS complaints
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`complaints` c
  JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments` s
    ON c.`shipment_id` = s.`shipment_id`
  WHERE c.`network_id` = 'NW-5809' AND s.`is_test` = FALSE
    AND c.`opened_date` >= DATE'2026-09-01' AND c.`opened_date` < DATE'2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
comp_all AS (
  SELECT date_format(`opened_date`, 'yyyy-MM') AS ym, COUNT(*) AS complaints
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`complaints`
  WHERE `network_id` = 'NW-5809'
    AND `opened_date` >= DATE'2026-09-01' AND `opened_date` < DATE'2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY 1
),
zone_detail AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(sh.ym, c.ym) AS ym, COALESCE(sh.`service_zone`, c.`service_zone`) AS zone,
         COALESCE(sh.shipments, 0) AS shipments, COALESCE(c.complaints, 0) AS complaints
  FROM ship_m sh
  FULL OUTER JOIN comp_m c ON sh.ym = c.ym AND sh.`service_zone` = c.`service_zone`
),
zone_rows AS (
  SELECT ym, zone, shipments, complaints,
         shipments * 1.0 / SUM(shipments) OVER (PARTITION BY ym) AS share_of_shipments,
         complaints * 1.0 / NULLIF(shipments, 0) AS complaint_rate
  FROM zone_detail
),
overall AS (
  SELECT t.ym, 'ALL' AS zone, t.shipments, COALESCE(c.complaints, 0) AS complaints,
         1.0 AS share_of_shipments,
         COALESCE(c.complaints, 0) * 1.0 / NULLIF(t.shipments, 0) AS complaint_rate
  FROM (SELECT ym, SUM(shipments) AS shipments FROM ship_m GROUP BY ym) t
  LEFT JOIN comp_all c ON t.ym = c.ym
)
SELECT ym, zone, shipments, complaints, ROUND(share_of_shipments * 100, 2) AS share_of_shipments_pct,
       ROUND(complaint_rate * 100, 3) AS complaint_rate_pct
FROM (SELECT * FROM overall UNION ALL SELECT * FROM zone_rows)
ORDER BY ym, CASE WHEN zone = 'ALL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, zone"}

| Month | Zone | Shipments | Share of shipments | Complaints | Complaint rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sep 2026 | All | 1,000 | 100% | 32 | 3.2% |
| Sep 2026 | Local | 800 | 80% | 16 | 2.0% |
| Sep 2026 | Remote | 200 | 20% | 16 | 8.0% |
| Oct 2026 | All | 1,000 | 100% | 58 | 5.8% |
| Oct 2026 | Local | 200 | 20% | 2 | 1.0% |
| Oct 2026 | Remote | 800 | 80% | 56 | 7.0% |

**What it shows**
- **Mix shift drove the overall increase.** Remote went from 20% to 80% of shipments. Applying September's zone rates to October's mix gives about 6.8%, so the overall rate would have risen even with no change in performance.
- **Within-zone rates improved.** Local fell from 2.0% to 1.0%, and remote fell from 8.0% to 7.0%. Holding the mix at September's levels, October's rates would give about 2.2% overall, below September's 3.2%.

question: For network NW-3378, compare the average delivery time in September and October 2026 for customer shipments only, leaving out internal test parcels (is_test). Did delivery time improve?

item.name: execute_sql
item.arguments:
{"title":"NW-3378 September vs October delivery time","sql":"WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_FORMAT(`ship_date`, 'yyyy-MM') AS `shipment_month`,
    AVG(`delivery_days`) AS `average_delivery_days`
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments`
  WHERE `network_id` = 'NW-3378'
    AND `is_test` = FALSE
    AND `ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
    AND `ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(`ship_date`, 'yyyy-MM')
), comparison AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN `shipment_month` = '2026-09' THEN `average_delivery_days` END) AS `september_average_delivery_days`,
    MAX(CASE WHEN `shipment_month` = '2026-10' THEN `average_delivery_days` END) AS `october_average_delivery_days`
  FROM monthly
)
SELECT
  `september_average_delivery_days`,
  `october_average_delivery_days`,
  `october_average_delivery_days` - `september_average_delivery_days` AS `change_days_october_minus_september`,
  CASE
    WHEN `october_average_delivery_days` < `september_average_delivery_days` THEN 'Improved'
    WHEN `october_average_delivery_days` > `september_average_delivery_days` THEN 'Worsened'
    ELSE 'No change'
  END AS `delivery_time_assessment`
FROM comparison"}

# NW-6731 shipment volume, September to October 2026

**The raw monthly totals show a 33% drop (900 to 600), but that is misleading. Like for like, volume rose about 33%.** October has data only through 15 October, so the two months don't cover the same number of days. The data can't tell us whether NW-6731 shipped anything after 15 October.

## Evidence
- **Monthly totals:** September has 900 shipments (1â30 Sep). October has 600 (1â15 Oct), a 33% drop in the raw total. No rows are test parcels or duplicates. Each month comes from a single load batch. \[[1](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca1291730bbfa6b4f16622061/chats/01f1d52f5fd0165faac443770b8ef4ab?gra_focus=pub_toolu_bdrk_01RBojMNxqsiXsR5ehMqHpDQ)\]
- **Same 15-day windows:** 1â15 Sep had 450 shipments and 16â30 Sep had 450. 1â15 Oct had 600, which is 33% above the same window in September. \[[2](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca1291730bbfa6b4f16622061/chats/01f1d52f5fd0165faac443770b8ef4ab?gra_focus=pub_toolu_bdrk_01BaPK6FiBThBcMETW6qH5MG)\]
- **Daily rate:** about 30 shipments a day in September against about 40 a day in the first half of October.
- **Missing second half of October:** NW-6731 has no shipments, invoices or complaints dated after 15 October. It also has no October invoices at all. \[[3](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca1291730bbfa6b4f16622061/chats/01f1d52f5fd0165faac443770b8ef4ab?gra_focus=pub_toolu_bdrk_016s13fg8TDKdtB9cKbpJWxC)\]
- **Other networks:** the company-wide data runs through 31 October. 13 other networks have shipments dated 16â31 October, against 14 networks in 1â15 October. NW-6731 stopping on 15 October therefore looks specific to this network. \[[3](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca1291730bbfa6b4f16622061/chats/01f1d52f5fd0165faac443770b8ef4ab?gra_focus=pub_toolu_bdrk_016s13fg8TDKdtB9cKbpJWxC)\]
- **No routing change:** the log has no routing changes for NW-6731, so nothing there explains a volume shift.

## Interpretation
Two explanations fit the data, and I can't separate them:
1. **The network's data is incomplete.** Its October load may have been cut off on 15 October. If it kept shipping at about 40 a day, October would be roughly 1,240 shipments, about 38% above September.
2. **The network really stopped shipping on 15 October.** In that case the real October total is 600, down 33% from September, after a stronger first half.

Check with the operations or data team whether NW-6731's October load is complete. Until then, treat the 900 to 600 drop as a data-coverage gap rather than a real decline.

{"title":"NW-1594 monthly complaint rate","sql":"WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    complaint_count,
    shipment_count,
    complaint_count * 100.0 / NULLIF(shipment_count, 0) AS complaints_per_100_shipments
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('month', s.`ship_date`) AS month_start,
      COUNT(DISTINCT c.`complaint_id`) AS complaint_count,
      COUNT(DISTINCT s.`shipment_id`) AS shipment_count
    FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`shipments` AS s
    LEFT JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`complaints` AS c
      ON c.`shipment_id` = s.`shipment_id`
    WHERE s.`network_id` = 'NW-1594'
      AND s.`ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
      AND s.`ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', s.`ship_date`)
  )
)
SELECT
  month_start,
  complaint_count,
  shipment_count,
  ROUND(complaints_per_100_shipments, 3) AS complaints_per_100_shipments,
  ROUND((complaints_per_100_shipments - LAG(complaints_per_100_shipments) OVER (ORDER BY month_start)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(LAG(complaints_per_100_shipments) OVER (ORDER BY month_start), 0), 1) AS rate_change_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month_start"}

Yesâcomplaints worsened materially in NW-1594 from September to October 2026.

- **Complaint volume rose 50%**, from **40 to 60 cases**.
- Shipments were unchanged at **1,000 per month**, so the complaint rate also rose from **4.0 to 6.0 complaints per 100 shipments**âa **50% increase**, not merely a result of higher shipment volume. \[[1](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca3d01b7fa19459fa7b3aa43d/chats/01f1d52f6370160a95c40bb7dfce5992?gra_focus=pub_call_vnFfttLMnk3Z9SWADVbwBnxM)\]

- The clearest operational concentration was **local shipments attributed to carrier capacity**, which rose from **12 complaints (2.0 per 100 local shipments)** to **37 (6.167 per 100)**. Remote complaints also increased from 16 to 23, so the deterioration was not limited exclusively to local service, but the local carrier-capacity segment drove most of the increase. \[[3](https://<workspace-host>/genie/rooms/01f1d52ca3d01b7fa19459fa7b3aa43d/chats/01f1d52f6370160a95c40bb7dfce5992?gra_focus=pub_call_yQdIUMGq3vsE13PJKC2ssgao)\]

**Conclusion:** October performance was clearly worse, with a higher normalized complaint rate and a strong shift toward late-delivery complaints, especially local carrier-capacity issues.

args.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    complaint_count,
    shipment_count,
    complaint_count * 100.0 / NULLIF(shipment_count, 0) AS complaints_per_100_shipments
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('month', s.`ship_date`) AS month_start,
      COUNT(DISTINCT c.`complaint_id`) AS complaint_count,
      COUNT(DISTINCT s.`shipment_id`) AS shipment_count
    FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`shipments` AS s
    LEFT JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`complaints` AS c
      ON c.`shipment_id` = s.`shipment_id`
    WHERE s.`network_id` = 'NW-1594'
      AND s.`ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
      AND s.`ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', s.`ship_date`)
  )
)
SELECT
  month_start,
  complaint_count,
  shipment_count,
  ROUND(complaints_per_100_shipments, 3) AS complaints_per_100_shipments,
  ROUND((complaints_per_100_shipments - LAG(complaints_per_100_shipments) OVER (ORDER BY month_start)) * 100.0 / NULLIF(LAG(complaints_per_100_shipments) OVER (ORDER BY month_start), 0), 1) AS rate_change_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month_start

WITH complaint_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', c.`opened_date`) AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS complaint_count
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`complaints` AS c
  WHERE c.`network_id` = 'NW-1594'
    AND c.`opened_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
    AND c.`opened_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', c.`opened_date`)
), shipment_zone_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', s.`ship_date`) AS month_start,
    s.`service_zone`,
    COUNT(*) AS shipment_count
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`shipments` AS s
  WHERE s.`network_id` = 'NW-1594'
    AND s.`ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
    AND s.`ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', s.`ship_date`), s.`service_zone`
), complaint_zone_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', c.`opened_date`) AS month_start,
    s.`service_zone`,
    COALESCE(s.`delay_reason`, 'on_time_or_unspecified') AS delay_reason,
    COUNT(*) AS complaint_count
  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`complaints` AS c
  JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel`.`shipments` AS s
    ON c.`shipment_id` = s.`shipment_id`
  WHERE c.`network_id` = 'NW-1594'
    AND c.`opened_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
    AND c.`opened_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', c.`opened_date`), s.`service_zone`, COALESCE(s.`delay_reason`, 'on_time_or_unspecified')
)
SELECT
  cm.`month_start`,
  cm.`complaint_count` AS total_complaints,
  SUM(sz.`shipment_count`) AS total_shipments,
  ROUND(cm.`complaint_count` * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(sz.`shipment_count`), 0), 3) AS complaints_per_100_shipments,
  cz.`service_zone`,
  cz.`delay_reason`,
  cz.`complaint_count` AS segment_complaints,
  MAX(CASE WHEN sz.`service_zone` = cz.`service_zone` THEN sz.`shipment_count` END) AS segment_shipments,
  ROUND(cz.`complaint_count` * 100.0 / NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN sz.`service_zone` = cz.`service_zone` THEN sz.`shipment_count` END), 0), 3) AS segment_complaints_per_100_shipments
FROM complaint_monthly cm

JOIN complaint_zone_monthly cz ON cz.`month_start` = cm.`month_start`

ORDER BY cm.`month_start`, segment_complaints DESC

{"title":"NW-1263 complaint rate comparison","sql":"WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    complaint_count,
    shipment_count,
    complaint_count / NULLIF(shipment_count, 0) AS complaint_rate
  FROM (
    SELECT
      'September 2026' AS month_label,
      (SELECT COUNT(*)
       FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`complaints` AS c
       WHERE c.`network_id` = 'NW-1263'
         AND c.`opened_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
         AND c.`opened_date` < DATE '2026-10-01') AS complaint_count,
      (SELECT COUNT(*)
       FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments` AS s
       WHERE s.`network_id` = 'NW-1263'
         AND s.`ship_date` >= DATE '2026-09-01'
         AND s.`ship_date` < DATE '2026-10-01'
         AND s.`is_test` = FALSE) AS shipment_count
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
      'October 2026' AS month_label,
      (SELECT COUNT(*)
       FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`complaints` AS c
       WHERE c.`network_id` = 'NW-1263'
         AND c.`opened_date` >= DATE '2026-10-01'
         AND c.`opened_date` < DATE '2026-11-01') AS complaint_count,
      (SELECT COUNT(*)
       FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`meridian_parcel_r2`.`shipments` AS s
       WHERE s.`network_id` = 'NW-1263'
         AND s.`ship_date` >= DATE '2026-10-01'
         AND s.`ship_date` < DATE '2026-11-01'
         AND s.`is_test` = FALSE) AS shipment_count
  )
), compared AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_label = 'September 2026' THEN complaint_rate END) AS september_rate,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_label = 'October 2026' THEN complaint_rate END) AS october_rate
  FROM monthly
)
SELECT
  m.`month_label`,
  m.`complaint_count`,
  m.`shipment_count`,
  m.`complaint_rate`,
  c.september_rate,
  c.october_rate,
  c.october_rate - c.september_rate AS rate_change,
  CASE
    WHEN c.october_rate > c.september_rate THEN 'Worse'
    WHEN c.october_rate < c.september_rate THEN 'Better'
    ELSE 'Unchanged'
  END AS conclusion
FROM monthly m
CROSS JOIN compared c
ORDER BY CASE WHEN m.`month_label` = 'September 2026' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END"}

{"title":"NW-1263 complaint rate and zone share, SepâOct 2026","sql":"WITH ship AS (
  SELECT date_format(ship_date,'yyyy-MM') AS ym, service_zone AS zone, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog.meridian_parcel_r2.shipments
  WHERE network_id='NW-1263' AND is_test=FALSE
    AND ship_date>=DATE'2026-09-01' AND ship_date<DATE'2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY 1,2
),
ship_tot AS (SELECT ym, SUM(n) AS n FROM ship GROUP BY ym),
comp_zone AS (
  SELECT date_format(c.opened_date,'yyyy-MM') AS ym, s.service_zone AS zone, COUNT(*) AS k
  FROM serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog.meridian_parcel_r2.complaints c
  JOIN serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog.meridian_parcel_r2.shipments s
    ON c.shipment_id=s.shipment_id AND s.is_test=FALSE
  WHERE c.network_id='NW-1263'
    AND c.opened_date>=DATE'2026-09-01' AND c.opened_date<DATE'2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY 1,2
),
comp_tot AS (
  SELECT date_format(opened_date,'yyyy-MM') AS ym, COUNT(*) AS k
  FROM serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog.meridian_parcel_r2.complaints
  WHERE network_id='NW-1263'
    AND opened_date>=DATE'2026-09-01' AND opened_date<DATE'2026-11-01'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT t.ym, 'All zones' AS zone, t.n AS shipments, COALESCE(ct.k,0) AS complaints,
